metadata.purpose: Index high-specificity evidence that bears directly on a person's documented denominational position, while preserving the distinction between signed positions, recorded votes, committee service, and first-person explanation.
metadata.modeling_rule: Formal position evidence is stronger for identifying a documented view than network proximity or generic event participation, but no evidence type should be collapsed into a total ideological label. Committee membership alone does not prove agreement with every line of a report, especially where a report records internal disagreement.

evidence_hierarchy.rule: A named signature on a formal report directly establishes support for the signed report position at that time, subject to any recorded qualification.
A recorded vote or signed protest directly establishes the recorded action, but not every broader theological inference someone might draw from it.
Use the speaker's actual stated position and preserve limits or qualifications rather than reducing the statement to a generic label.
Committee service on a consensus report establishes participation in producing the report. It does not prove agreement with every sentence or resolve internal alternatives unless the source says so.
Institutional service alone is not a substitute for a person's documented view.
Participation establishes the participation event only and must not be used as a proxy for agreement with every position associated with the event or network.

normalized_position_sources.coverage: complete published committee roster plus report-level position boundaries and one first-person committee-member statement
normalized_position_sources.important_boundary: The published report says the committee reached an overwhelming consensus but also records two schools of thought on women teaching men; do not infer which school an individual member held without separate evidence.

normalized_position_sources.coverage: reviewed user-supplied transcript of first-person explanatory video
normalized_position_sources.important_boundary: Use McGreevy's explicit statements rather than attributing every committee-report sentence to her.
The protest objected to specified language/action and must not be reduced to generic support for or opposition to Revoice.

normalized_position_sources.coverage: official committee roster; report-position extraction remains a separate future pass
normalized_position_sources.important_boundary: Committee membership is not automatically treated as agreement with every later interpretation or use of the report.
A recorded negative vote establishes the vote, not a complete account of the commissioner's rationale.
Protest signership records objection to the PCA withdrawal action and should not be generalized beyond the protest's stated grounds.

priority_backlog.target: Corresponding majority/committee reports for controversies where a minority report is already normalized
priority_backlog.reason: Majority and minority positions should be represented symmetrically when the official minutes identify named authors, signers, committee members, or recorded votes.

priority_backlog.target: Major PCA study reports with identifiable committee members, concurrences, dissents, minority reports, or signed recommendations
priority_backlog.reason: These sources provide high-specificity evidence of documented denominational positions and should be normalized before lower-signal network expansion.

priority_backlog.target: First-person explanations by report authors, signers, or dissenters
priority_backlog.reason: These can clarify the person's actual rationale where a formal vote or committee role alone is underdetermined.
